name: Direct Prompt-Injection Attack Taxonomy
executive_summary: The earliest systematic catalog of direct prompt-injection attack techniques — naming and classifying how attacker-supplied text can override a system's intended instructions.
description: Establishes prompt injection as a named phenomenon: an attacker embeds text in the user-controlled portion of a prompt that is crafted to be interpreted as a new instruction, overriding or leaking the system's original instructions. Catalogs specific attack techniques (e.g. goal hijacking, prompt leaking). Foundational threat model for any system's adversarial-resilience design.
when_to_use: Threat-modeling any system that inserts untrusted user text into a prompt alongside system instructions.
when_not_to_use: N/A — this is threat-model background, not an applied generation technique.
known_pitfalls: Understanding the taxonomy is necessary but not sufficient for defense; naming an attack class doesn't by itself neutralize it.

primary_source.title: Ignore Previous Prompt: Attack Techniques for Language Models
primary_source.venue: arXiv preprint / NeurIPS ML Safety Workshop 2022

variables.name: untrusted_user_content
variables.description: User-supplied text that could contain an injection attempt

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
